# Level 1 Student Handout: Purification & Prayer

| Metadata Field | Curriculum Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Target Age Group** | Ages 6-8 (Level 1 Track: Primary Stage 1) |
| **Estimated Study Time** | 45-60 minutes |
| **Prerequisites** | Foundational understanding of Allah as the Creator and knowing how to listen attentively |
| **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6): The Command for Ablution before Prayer |
| **Tajweed Rule** | Natural Prolongation (Madd Tabi'i: stretching vowel sounds for two counts) |
| **Classical Text Anchor** | *Mukhtasar al-Akhdari* (The Foundations of Purification and Prayer) by Imam al-Akhdari |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 10: "Allah is Pure and Accepts Only What Is Pure" (Sahih Muslim 1015) |

---

## Section 1: Cleanliness is Half of Faith

Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught us a golden rule for our daily life:

> **الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ**  
> *"Cleanliness is half of faith."* (Sahih Muslim 223, Sahih).

Allah loves children who are clean, neat, and fresh. A Muslim takes care of their body, brushes their teeth every morning and evening, clips their nails, washes their hands before eating, and wears clean clothes.

When we prepare to stand before Allah in prayer, we perform a special wash called **Wudu** (ablution). Wudu washes away physical dust and brings light, joy, and peace into our hearts.

---

## Section 2: Bathroom Manners (Istinja and Istijmar)

Islam teaches us polite, healthy manners for every part of our day, including using the washroom:

1. **Enter with your left foot** and say the protection du'a:  
   *“Bismillah, Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-khubthi wal-khaba'ith”*  
   (In the name of Allah; O Allah, I seek refuge in You from all foul and harmful things). (Sahih al-Bukhari 142, Sahih Muslim 375, Sahih).
2. **Keep clean:** Take care that no drops or dirt splash onto your clothes or body.
3. **Wash with pure water:** Clean yourself thoroughly using clean water (*Istinja*) with your left hand. If water is not immediately available, clean dry paper or stones may be used to remove impurities (*Istijmar*).
4. **Exit with your right foot** and say:  
   *“Ghufranak”*  
   (O Allah, I ask for Your forgiveness and thank You for relief). (Sunan Abi Dawud 30, Jami' at-Tirmidhi 7, Sahih).
5. **Wash your hands with soap and water** so your hands are clean and fresh.

---

## Section 3: The Seven Essential Steps of Wudu (Fara'id al-Wudu)

In the Maliki school, following the practice of the Prophet ﷺ and the people of Madinah, there are **seven essential steps** (*Fara'id*). If any of these seven steps is missed, the wudu is not complete and must be corrected:

| Step Number | Obligatory Action (*Fard*) | How to Perform It |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **Intention (*Al-Niyyah*)** | Make the intention in your heart to perform wudu for the pleasure of Allah. |
| **2** | **Washing the Face (*Ghasl al-Wajh*)** | Wash your entire face, from the normal hairline down to the chin, and from earlobe to earlobe. |
| **3** | **Washing the Arms (*Ghasl al-Yadayn*)** | Wash both hands and arms thoroughly, starting from the fingertips up to and including the elbows. |
| **4** | **Wiping the Head (*Mash al-Ra's*)** | Wet your hands and wipe your entire head from the forehead back to the nape of the neck. |
| **5** | **Washing the Feet (*Ghasl al-Rijlayn*)** | Wash both feet thoroughly up to and including the ankle-bones, making sure water passes between the toes. |
| **6** | **Gentle Rubbing (*Al-Dalk*)** | Pass your wet hand gently over each limb while washing with water so the water reaches all the skin. |
| **7** | **Continuity (*Al-Muwalat*)** | Wash each limb right after the other without taking long breaks in between. |

---

## Section 4: Sunnahs and Meritorious Acts (Sunan wa Fada'il)

In addition to the seven obligations, our Prophet ﷺ taught us beautiful actions that bring extra reward and make our wudu complete:

* **Saying Bismillah (Meritorious Act / *Fadilah*):** We begin our wudu by saying *Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim* (In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful).
* **Washing hands to the wrists (Sunnah):** Wash your hands three times before dipping them into the water basin.
* **Rinsing the mouth (*Madmadah* - Sunnah):** Take fresh water into your mouth, swirl it around, and spit it out gently three times.
* **Sniffing and blowing out water (*Istinshaq* and *Istinthar* - Sunnah):** Sniff clean water into your nostrils and blow it out gently three times.
* **Wiping the ears (Sunnah):** Wipe the inside and outside of both ears using fresh, moist fingers.
* **Returning the head wipe (*Radd al-Mash* - Sunnah):** Bring your wet hands forward from the nape of the neck back to the forehead.
* **Washing three times (*Al-Tathlith* - Meritorious Act / *Fadilah*):** Washing each limb three times is beloved and meritorious, while washing once thoroughly with rubbing is the obligatory minimum.

---

## Section 5: The Five Daily Prayers: Our Golden Meetings with Allah

Every day, Muslims around the world hear the call to prayer (*Adhan*) and stand facing the Holy Ka'bah in Makkah to perform the **Five Daily Prayers**:

| Prayer Name | When We Pray | Number of Rak'ahs | How We Recite |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Fajr** | Before sunrise at dawn | **2 Rak'ahs** | Recited aloud |
| **Dhuhr** | Midday, after the sun passes its peak | **4 Rak'ahs** | Recited quietly |
| **'Asr** | Late afternoon before sunset | **4 Rak'ahs** | Recited quietly |
| **Maghrib** | Right after sunset | **3 Rak'ahs** | First 2 rak'ahs aloud, 3rd rak'ah quiet |
| **'Isha** | Nighttime when darkness settles | **4 Rak'ahs** | First 2 rak'ahs aloud, last 2 rak'ahs quiet |

### The Movements of Salah: Standing in Respect
When we stand before Allah, our whole body expresses reverence and humility:
* **The Opening Takbir (*Takbirat al-Ihram*):** We raise our hands to shoulder or ear level and say: *"Allahu Akbar"* (Allah is Greater than all things).
* **Standing (*Qiyam*):** In the Maliki school, we stand with our arms resting naturally and gently at our sides (*Sadl*), keeping our body relaxed, still, and respectful.
* **Bowing (*Ruku'*):** We bow with a straight back, place our hands on our knees, and say three times: *"Subhana Rabbiy al-'Azim"* (Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent).
* **Prostration (*Sujud*):** We place our forehead, nose, palms, knees, and toes on the clean floor and say three times: *"Subhana Rabbiy al-A'la"* (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High). This is the closest a servant comes to Allah.
* **Sitting (*Jalsah*):** We sit peacefully and recite the *Tashahhud* and blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

---

## Section 6: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 1. Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6)
Allah commands us in the Holy Qur'an:

> **يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ**  
> *Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu idha qumtum ila al-salati faghsilu wujuhakum wa aydiyakum ila al-marafiqi wamsahu bi-ru'usikum wa arjulakum ila al-ka'bayn.*  
> *"O you who believe! When you rise up for prayer, wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles."* (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6).

**Classical Tafsir (*Tafsir al-Qurtubi*):** Imam al-Qurtubi explains that this noble verse is the divine foundation of wudu. It lists the essential bodily limbs that must be washed before prayer, showing that inner purity of the heart begins with outer purification of the body.

### 2. Tajweed Rule in Action: Natural Prolongation (Madd Tabi'i)
*Madd Tabi'i* (natural stretch) occurs when a vowel letter (Alif after Fathah, Waw after Dammah, or Ya after Kasrah) appears without a Hamzah or Sukun after it. It is held for exactly two vowel counts (beats).  
* Examples from Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6:
  * In the word **آمَنُوا** (*amanu*), the Alif and Waw are stretched naturally for two counts.
  * In the word **أَقَامُوا** (*aqamu*), the Alif is held for two counts without rushing or over-stretching.

### 3. Classical Maliki Text Anchor: *Mukhtasar al-Akhdari*
Imam Abu Zayd 'Abd al-Rahman al-Akhdari (d. 983 AH) writes in his foundational manual of Maliki fiqh:
> *"The obligations (Fara'id) of Wudu are seven: intention (Niyyah), washing the face, washing the arms up to the elbows, wiping the entire head, washing the feet up to the ankles, gentle rubbing (Dalk), and continuity (Muwalat)."*

Imam al-Akhdari emphasizes that learning these seven pillars ensures our prayers are built on sound, valid foundations from childhood.

### 4. Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 10 of Nawawi's 40
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

> **إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا**  
> *"Indeed, Allah the Exalted is Pure, and He accepts only that which is pure."* (Sahih Muslim 1015, Sahih).

**Family Application:** When we wash for prayer, eat wholesome lawful food, and speak truthful words, we offer Allah what is pure and beloved to Him. Cleanliness in our room, our clothes, and our speech brings peace and blessings into our family home.

# Level 1 Activity Sheet: Purification & Prayer

## Part A: Multiple Choice Questions

1. What is the special wash we perform with clean water before standing in prayer?
   (A) Tayammum
   (B) Wudu
   (C) Suhoor
   (D) Zakah

2. Which direction do Muslims all over the world face when standing in prayer?
   (A) Toward the rising sun in the east
   (B) Toward the nearest mountain range
   (C) Toward the local community center
   (D) Toward the Holy Ka'bah in Makkah (the Qiblah)

3. In the Maliki school, how do we wipe our head during Wudu?
   (A) Wiping gently over the whole head from the front hairline to the nape of the neck
   (B) Touching only three hairs at the front with one fingertip
   (C) Washing the head with shampoo and warm water
   (D) Wiping only the back of the neck and ears

4. What is the special Maliki obligation in Wudu where we gently pass our wet hand over each limb?
   (A) Al-Muwalat (continuity)
   (B) Al-Niyyah (intention)
   (C) Al-Dalk (gentle rubbing)
   (D) Al-Tartib (following order)

5. What do we whisper with reverence when we place our forehead on the floor in Sujud?
   (A) Subhana Rabbiy al-'Azim
   (B) Subhana Rabbiy al-A'la
   (C) Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'Alamin
   (D) Astaghfirullah wa Atubu Ilayh

---

## Part B: Fill in the Blanks

Vocabulary Bank: Wudu, Qiblah, Sadl, Dalk, Fajr

6. The direction toward the Ka'bah that Muslims face in prayer is called the ______.
7. Before we stand in prayer, we perform ______ with clean water to wash our limbs.
8. Resting our arms naturally and gently at our sides during prayer is called ______.
9. The morning prayer prayed before sunrise consisting of two rak'ahs is ______.
10. Gently rubbing each limb with water during wudu is called ______.

---

## Part C: Matching Terms

* Al-Dalk ─── Passing the wet hand gently over each limb during wudu
* The Qiblah ─── The direction toward the Holy Ka'bah in Makkah
* Sujud ─── Touching the forehead and nose to the ground in worship
* Sadl ─── Standing with arms resting naturally at the sides in prayer
* Fajr ─── The two-rak'ah dawn prayer recited aloud

---

## Part D: Reflection & Application

11. Describe how you feel after making a fresh, cool wudu, and why cleanliness helps us prepare to talk to Allah.

---

## Answer Key & Marking Guide

1. B - Wudu is the special ritual wash performed with clean water before standing in prayer.
2. D - All Muslims face the Holy Ka'bah in Makkah, which is known as the Qiblah.
3. A - In the Maliki school, wiping the entire head from the front hairline to the nape of the neck is an obligatory pillar (Fard).
4. C - Al-Dalk is the gentle rubbing of each limb with the wet hand during wudu.
5. B - In Sujud (prostration), we say Subhana Rabbiy al-A'la (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High) three times.

### Fill in the Blanks Key
6. Qiblah - The direction toward Makkah.
7. Wudu - The ritual wash before prayer.
8. Sadl - Standing with arms resting naturally at the sides.
9. Fajr - The two-rak'ah morning prayer.
10. Dalk - Rubbing the limb with water.

### Matching Key
* Al-Dalk connects with Passing the wet hand gently over each limb during wudu.
* The Qiblah connects with The direction toward the Holy Ka'bah in Makkah.
* Sujud connects with Touching the forehead and nose to the ground in worship.
* Sadl connects with Standing with arms resting naturally at the sides in prayer.
* Fajr connects with The two-rak'ah dawn prayer recited aloud.

### Reflection Marking Rubric
- Question 11: Awards full credit for expressing that wudu cleans both the body and heart, helping a child feel peaceful, calm, and respectful before standing to pray to Allah.

Natural bodily emissions from the private exits (urine, stool, passing gas, pre-seminal fluid). 2. Deep, heavy sleep where a person loses conscious awareness of sounds and movement around them. 3. Complete loss of consciousness (fainting, deep dizziness, or anesthesia). ### Things that DO NOT Break Wudu in Maliki Fiqh: * Eating food of any kind, including cooked camel meat (the Hanbali school views camel meat as breaking wudu, whereas Malikis, Hanafis, and Shafi'is hold that it does not). * Minor bleeding from cuts, scratches, or nosebleeds. * Light drowsiness or nodding off where you can still hear people speaking around you. * Touching clean animals or everyday objects. --- ## Section 4: The Five Conditions (Shurut) for a Valid Prayer Before raising your hands for the opening Takbir, five mandatory conditions must be fulfilled: 1. **Purity (*Taharah*):** Being pure from minor ritual impurity (through Wudu) and major ritual impurity (through Ghusl), and ensuring body, clothing, and prayer space are free from physical filth (*Khabath*). 2. **Covering the 'Awrah:** Boys must cover from the navel to the knee with loose, non-transparent clothing; girls cover their entire body except for the face and hands. 3. **Facing the Qiblah:** Aligning your chest toward the Sacred Ka'bah in Makkah. 4. **Entry of the Prayer Time:** Praying within the prescribed time window. A prayer performed before its time enters is completely invalid. 5. **Intention (*Al-Niyyah*):** Knowing with certainty in your heart which specific prayer you are about to perform (such as Dhuhr today for the pleasure of Allah). --- ## Section 5: The Five Daily Prayers and the Maliki Posture of Standing The five daily prayers form the spiritual rhythm of our day: | Prayer Name | Prayer Time | Number of Rak'ahs | Recitation Method | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Fajr** | Dawn before sunrise | **2 Rak'ahs** | Recited aloud | | **Dhuhr** | Midday, after the sun passes its zenith | **4 Rak'ahs** | Recited quietly | | **'Asr** | Late afternoon before sunset | **4 Rak'ahs** | Recited quietly | | **Maghrib** | Immediately after sunset | **3 Rak'ahs** | First 2 rak'ahs aloud, 3rd rak'ah quiet | | **'Isha** | Nighttime after twilight fades | **4 Rak'ahs** | First 2 rak'ahs aloud, last 2 rak'ahs quiet | ### Standing in Prayer: Sadl and Qabd In the standing position (*Qiyam*) of obligatory prayers, the relied-upon position in the Maliki school is **Sadl** (resting the arms naturally and gently at the sides). * **Why do Malikis practice Sadl?** Imam Malik lived and taught in Madinah, the city of the Prophet ﷺ. He observed that the scholars, elders, and descendants of the Companions in Madinah stood with their arms naturally at their sides during obligatory prayers. This continuous living communal practice (*'Amal Ahl al-Madinah*) was a strong proof of the Sunnah. * **What about Qabd?** Clasping the right hand over the left wrist or forearm (*Qabd*) is also an authentic Sunni practice narrated in hadith. In the Maliki school, *Qabd* is permitted in voluntary prayers. Both *Sadl* and *Qabd* are respected, valid Sunnahs, and Muslims should pray together with love, unity, and mutual respect in every mosque. ### The Reward of Congregational Prayer (Salat al-Jama'ah) The Prophet ﷺ said: > *"Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times superior to praying alone."* (Sahih al-Bukhari 645, Sahih Muslim 650, Sahih). --- ## Section 6: Curriculum Anchors in Practice ### 1. Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Bayyinah (98:5) and Al-Ma'idah (5:6) Allah states: > **وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ** > *Wa ma umiru illa li-ya'budu Allaha mukhlisina lahu al-dina hunafa'a wa yuqimu al-salata wa yu'tu al-zakata wa dhalika dinu al-qayyimah.* > *"And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, upright, and to establish prayer and give Zakah. And that is the correct religion."* (Surah Al-Bayyinah 98:5). **Classical Tafsir (*Tafsir Ibn Juzayy al-Kalbi*):** Ibn Juzayy explains that this verse proves that physical actions of prayer and purity are worthless without sincere inner intention (*Ikhlas*). Purity of the heart must accompany the washing of the body. ### 2. Tajweed Rule in Action: The Echo Letters (Qalqalah) *Qalqalah* is a bouncing, echoing sound produced when one of the five letters of Qalqalah carries a Sukun (quiescent letter) or when stopping at the end of a word: * The five letters are grouped in the phrase: **قُطْبُ جَدٍّ** (*Qaf, Ta, Ba, Jim, Dal*). * Examples: * In Surah Al-Bayyinah (98:8): **تَجْرِي** (*taj-ri*): The letter Jim has a gentle bounce (*Qalqalah Sughra*). * In Surah Al-Falaq (113:1): **الْفَلَقِ** (*al-falaq*): When stopping on Qaf, it receives a clear bounce (*Qalqalah Kubra*). * In Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1): **أَحَدٌ** (*ahad*): When stopping on Dal, it bounces clearly. ### 3. Classical Maliki Text Anchor: *Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah* Imam 'Abd al-Bari al-'Ashmawi writes in *Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah*: > *"Know that water which is valid for purification is pure water (Ma' Tahur), which has not been altered in color, taste, or odor by anything that separates from it. The obligations of wudu are seven: intention, washing the face, washing the arms to the elbows, wiping the whole head, washing the feet to the ankles, rubbing, and continuity."* ### 4. Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 2 of Nawawi's 40 (Hadith of Jibril) Sayyidina 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) narrated that Angel Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ replied: > **الْإِسْلَامُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَتُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِيَ الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجَّ الْبَيْتَ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا** > *"Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to give Zakah, to fast Ramadan, and to perform the pilgrimage to the House if you have the means."* (Sahih Muslim 8, Sahih). **Family Application:** Prayer is the visible pillar of our Islam. Setting a family prayer routine where parents and children pray together in congregation fills our home with light, strengthens bonds between siblings, and instills lifelong discipline.

| Metadata Field | Curriculum Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Target Age Group** | Ages 10-12 (Level 3 Track: Years 5 & 6) |
| **Estimated Study Time** | 75-90 minutes |
| **Prerequisites** | Level 2 mastery of Wudu obligations, basic conditions of prayer, and water taxonomy |
| **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6) and Surah Al-Inshiqaq (84:1-6): Physical and Spiritual Accounting |
| **Tajweed Rule** | The Four Rules of Noon Sakinah and Tanween (Izhar, Idgham, Iqlab, Ikhfa') |
| **Classical Text Spine** | *Matn Ibn 'Ashir* (*Al-Murshid al-Mu'in*, lines 48-59, 75-85, 115-125) and *Mukhtasar al-Akhdari* |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 3: The Five Pillars of Islam (Sahih al-Bukhari 8, Sahih Muslim 16) |

---

## Section 1: The Fiqh of Purity: Approaching the Divine Presence

At ages 10 to 12, your daily prayer (*Salah*) transitions into a conscious, mature covenant with Allah. In Islamic jurisprudence, ritual purity (*Taharah*) is divided into two distinct dimensions:

1. **Purification from Minor Ritual Impurity (*Hadath Asghar*):** Lifted by performing complete Wudu with pure water.
2. **Purification from Major Ritual Impurity (*Hadath Akbar*):** Lifted by performing the complete ritual bath (*Ghusl*) with pure water.

Purity also requires the complete removal of physical filth (*Khabath*, such as urine, stool, or spilled blood) from three places: your body, your clothing, and the physical surface upon which you prostrate.

---

## Section 2: The Seven Obligations of Wudu in Matn Ibn 'Ashir

In his celebrated classical didactic poem *Al-Murshid al-Mu'in 'ala al-Daruri min 'Ulum al-Din*, Imam 'Abd al-Wahid ibn 'Ashir (d. 1040 AH) states lines 48-50 on the obligations (*Fara'id*) of Wudu:

> **فَصْلٌ فَرَائِضُ الْوُضُوءِ سَبْعُ *** وَهْيَ دَلْكٌ فَوْرٌ نِيَّةٌ فِي بَدْءِ**  
> **وَغَسْلُ وَجْهٍ غَسْلُهُ الْيَدَيْنِ *** وَمَسْحُ رَأْسٍ غَسْلُهُ الرِّجْلَيْنِ**  
> **وَالْفَرْضُ عَمَّ مَجْمَعَ الأُذْنَيْنِ *** وَالْمِرْفَقَيْنِ عَمَّ وَالْكَعْبَيْنِ**  
> *"Section: The obligations of Wudu are seven: rubbing (Dalk), continuity (Fawr), intention (Niyyah) at the beginning, washing the face, washing the two hands and arms, wiping the head, and washing the two feet. And the obligation encompasses the boundary meeting the two ears, and includes the two elbows and the two ankle-bones."*

### Detailed Explanation of the Seven Fara'id:
1. **Intention (*Al-Niyyah*):** Formed silently in the heart at the very first obligatory wash (washing the face), intending either to lift ritual impurity (*Raf' al-Hadath*) or to make prayer permissible (*Istibahat al-Salah*).
2. **Washing the Face (*Ghasl al-Wajh*):** From the normal top hairline to the bottom of the chin, and horizontally from earlobe to earlobe (the phrase *majma' al-udhnayn* refers to the facial boundary next to the ears; the ears themselves are washed as a Sunnah, not a Fard).
3. **Washing the Arms (*Ghasl al-Yadayn*):** Washing both hands and forearms from the fingertips up to and including the elbows (*Al-Mirfaqayn*).
4. **Wiping the Entire Head (*Mash Jami' al-Ra's*):** Moistening both hands and wiping the entire skull from the front hairline all the way back to the nape of the neck. (Returning the hands back to the front, *Radd al-Mash*, is an emphasized Sunnah).
5. **Washing the Feet (*Ghasl al-Rijlayn*):** Washing both feet up to and including the ankle-bones (*Al-Ka'bayn*), ensuring water penetrates between all toes.
6. **Gentle Rubbing (*Al-Dalk*):** Passing the hand over each limb while or immediately after pouring water. This ensures the water cleanses the skin directly rather than merely sliding off. Rubbing is a unique obligation in the Maliki school.
7. **Continuity (*Al-Muwalat* or *Al-Fawr*):** Washing consecutive limbs without allowing the preceding limb to dry under normal, moderate weather conditions. (Note: Continuity is obligatory in both the Maliki and Hanbali schools, while the Shafi'i and Hanafi schools classify it as a Sunnah).

---

## Section 3: Nullifiers of Wudu (Nawaqid al-Wudu)

The Maliki school categorizes things that break wudu into two clear divisions:

### 1. Actual Events (*Ahdath*):
* Direct discharges from the private passages: urine, stool, wind, pre-seminal fluid (*Madhy*), and post-urinary prostatic fluid (*Wady*).

### 2. Indirect Causes (*Asbab*):
* Loss of intellect or awareness:
  * Heavy, deep sleep where you lose complete awareness (dropping an item from your hand without noticing).
  * Fainting, intoxication, medication, or temporary loss of consciousness.
* Touching with sexual desire: In the Maliki school, touching an adult of the opposite gender breaks wudu only if it is accompanied by pleasure or intended for pleasure. Casual contact without desire (such as a child bumping into a relative or a doctor examining a patient) does not invalidate wudu.

### Wiping Over Leather Footwear (*Mash 'ala al-Khuffayn*):
If a person wears sturdy leather socks or boots that cover the ankles:
* The footwear must have been put on while in a complete state of purity established by washing with water.
* When performing wudu, the person may wipe over the top of the footwear with moistened hands instead of removing them to wash the feet.
* In the Maliki school, there is no fixed time limit for wiping over leather socks, provided the wearer does not enter a state of major ritual impurity (*Janabah*) and does not take them off.

---

## Section 4: Ghusl and Tayammum: Purification with Sa'id

### 1. The Fiqh of Ghusl (The Major Ritual Bath):
Ghusl is required after major ritual impurity (such as marital relations, nocturnal emission, or the completion of post-natal bleeding and menstruation).  
* **The Fara'id of Ghusl in Maliki Fiqh:**
  1. Intention (*Niyyah*) in the heart to lift major ritual impurity (*Raf' al-Hadath al-Akbar*).
  2. Continuity (*Al-Muwalat*).
  3. Rubbing (*Al-Dalk*) the entire body with the hand.
  4. Pouring water over every part of the body, including roots of hair.
  5. Picking through thick hair and skin folds (*Takhlil*) so water touches the skin beneath.

### 2. Tayammum (Dry Ablution with Earth):
When water is genuinely unavailable after searching, or when using water would cause medical harm or severe illness, Allah permits Tayammum:
* **The Substance (*Sa'id*):** Tayammum must be performed on pure, unadulterated natural earth (*Sa'id*), such as natural stone, rock, clean soil, or sand.
* **The Method in Maliki Fiqh:**
  1. Form the intention to render prayer permissible (*Istibahat al-Salah*).
  2. Strike the clean stone or earth once with both palms.
  3. Wipe the entire face once (*Fard*).
  4. Wipe both hands up to the wrists (*Fard*).
  5. It is an emphasized Sunnah to strike the stone a second time and wipe from the wrists up to the elbows.

---

## Section 5: The Call to Prayer: The Madinan Adhan with Tarji'

The Maliki Adhan preserves the historical call to prayer delivered by Sayyidina Bilal ibn Rabah in the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah:
* **The Opening Takbir:** The Madinan Adhan begins with **two** Takbirs (*Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar*), rather than four.
* **Al-Tarji' (التَّرْجِيع):** The Mu'adhin recites the two testimonies of faith (*Ash-hadu alla ilaha illallah*, *Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah*) softly to himself first, and then repeats them aloud with full vocal power. This brings the total count of the Maliki Adhan to 17 phrases.
* **The Iqamah:** The Maliki Iqamah consists of 10 concise phrases. Every sentence is uttered once, including the phrase *Qad qamat al-salah* (said once), while the opening and closing Takbirs are paired (*Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar*).

---

## Section 6: Sujud al-Sahw Clinic: Repairing Prayer Mistakes

Because human beings are prone to distraction or forgetfulness, Allah established a precise, logical legal mechanism to repair prayer errors:

### 1. Sujud al-Qabli (الْقَبْلِيُّ: Before the Final Salam):
* **When is it performed?** When you accidentally **omit (subtract / *Nuqsan*)** two or more confirmed sunnahs from the prayer (such as forgetting the middle Tashahhud and standing directly up for the third rak'ah).
* **The Exact Method in Relied-upon Maliki Fiqh (*Matn Ibn 'Ashir*, *Mukhtasar al-Akhdari*):**
  * Complete your normal final Tashahhud and blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ.
  * *Before* saying the Salam, make two prostrations (*Sajdatayn*), saying *Allahu Akbar* for each movement.
  * Sit up from the second prostration and **immediately say the Salam to conclude your prayer**.
  * **Critical Maliki Rule:** There is **NO second Tashahhud** recited after *Sujud al-Qabli*. You recite the Tashahhud once before the prostrations, prostrate twice, and immediately give the final Salam.

### 2. Sujud al-Ba'di (الْبَعْدِيُّ: After the Final Salam):
* **When is it performed?** When you accidentally **add (*Ziyadah*)** an extra action to the prayer (such as an extra bowing, an extra prostration, or standing for a fifth rak'ah by mistake).
* **The Exact Method:**
  * Complete the prayer normally, make the final Salam, and sit.
  * Say *Allahu Akbar* and perform two prostrations of forgetfulness.
  * Sit up, recite a second Tashahhud, and say Salam a second time to complete the rectification.

### 3. Combining Omission and Addition:
If you both omitted a sunnah and added an extra action during the same prayer, **the omission takes priority**, and you perform **Sujud al-Qabli** before the Salam.

### 4. Handling Doubt (*Shakk*):
If you doubt whether you have prayed three or four rak'ahs, apply the classical legal maxim: *"Certainty is not dispelled by doubt"* (*Al-Yaqinu la yazulu bish-Shakk*).  
* Build upon certainty (the lower number: 3 rak'ahs).
* Pray the remaining fourth rak'ah.
* Because you may have actually prayed five rak'ahs, complete the prayer, say the final Salam, and perform **Sujud al-Ba'di** after the Salam.

---

## Section 7: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 1. Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Inshiqaq (84:1-6)
Allah warns us of our ultimate meeting:

> **يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ**  
> *Ya ayyuha al-insanu innaka kadihun ila rabbika kadhan fa-mulaqih.*  
> *"O human being! Indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with strenuous labor, and you will surely meet Him."* (Surah Al-Inshiqaq 84:6).

**Classical Tafsir (*Tafsir al-Qurtubi*):** Imam al-Qurtubi writes that every soul is striving toward its Creator day by day. Prayer is the scheduled spiritual checkpoint where we stand before Allah in this world before our ultimate accounting on the Day of Judgment.

### 2. Tajweed Rule in Action: The Four Rules of Noon Sakinah and Tanween
When a Noon Sakinah (نْ) or Tanween (ً ٍ ٌ) is followed by an Arabic letter, one of four rules applies:
1. **Izhar Halqi (Clear Pronunciation):** Pronounced clearly before the six throat letters: Hamzah, Ha, 'Ayn, Ha, Ghayn, Kha. Example: **مَنْ آمَنَ** (*man amana*).
2. **Idgham (Merging):** Merged into the six letters of *Yarmalun* (ي ر م ل و ن):
   * *Idgham bi-Ghunnah* (with nasal tone) for letters: Ya, Noon, Meem, Waw. Example: **مَن يَقُولُ** (*may-yaqul*).
   * *Idgham bila Ghunnah* (without nasal tone) for letters: Lam and Ra. Example: **مِن رَّبِّهِمْ** (*mir-rabbihim*).
3. **Iqlab (Conversion):** Converted into a hidden Meem with a nasal hum before the letter Ba. Example: **مِن بَعْدِ** (*mim-ba'd*).
4. **Ikhfa' Haqiqi (Concealment):** Pronounced with a light nasal hum before the remaining 15 letters. Example: **مِن قَبْلِ** (*min-qabl*).

### 3. Classical Maliki Text Anchor: *Matn Ibn 'Ashir*
Lines 117-118 of *Al-Murshid al-Mu'in* summarize the prostration of omission:
> **قَبْلَ السَّلاَمِ سَجْدَتَانِ يَسْجُدُ *** إِنْ نَقَصَتْ سُنَّتُهُ لاَ يَشْهَدُ**  
> **وَبَعْدَهُ يَسْجُدُ إِنْ تَزِيدُ *** مُتَشَهِّدًا لِخَتْمِهِ يُعِيدُ**  
> *"Before the Salam two prostrations are made if a Sunnah was decreased, and he does not recite Tashahhud. And after it he prostrates if he added, reciting Tashahhud and repeating the concluding Salam."*

### 4. Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 3 of Nawawi's 40
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

> **بُنِيَ الْإِسْلَامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ، وَحَجِّ الْبَيْتِ، وَصَوْمِ رَمَضَانَ**  
> *"Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving Zakah, performing pilgrimage to the House, and fasting Ramadan."* (Sahih al-Bukhari 8, Sahih Muslim 16, Sahih).

**Family Application:** Establishing prayer (*Iqamat al-Salah*) means more than praying quickly; it means perfecting wudu, learning the rulings of repair (*Sujud al-Sahw*), and maintaining concentration (*Khushu'*). When children learn how to fix mistakes in prayer, they gain confidence and peace of mind before Allah.

## Part A: Multiple Choice Questions

1. How many obligatory acts (Fara'id) of Wudu are codified in the classical Maliki text *Matn Ibn 'Ashir*?
   (A) Four obligations
   (B) Five obligations
   (C) Six obligations
   (D) Seven obligations

   (A) Washing the face and washing the arms to elbows
   (B) Rubbing the limbs (Al-Dalk) and continuity without delay (Al-Muwalat)
   (C) Wiping the ears and rinsing the mouth
   (D) Washing the hands to the wrists and using a siwak

3. What is the exact facial boundary (*Ghasl al-Wajh*) that must be washed during Wudu?
   (A) From the normal top hairline to the bottom of the chin, and from earlobe to earlobe
   (B) From the eyebrows to the bottom of the lower lip only
   (C) From the top of the forehead to the bridge of the nose
   (D) The entire head including the ears and the nape of the neck

4. When performing Tayammum in the absence of water, what substance is legally classified as *Sa'id* in the Maliki school?
   (A) Any dry cloth, wool carpet, or clean blanket
   (B) Processed clay tiles treated with chemical glaze
   (C) Pure natural earth, uncarved stone, rock, or clean sand
   (D) Purified ash or charcoal from wood fires

5. What is the distinct characteristic of *Al-Tarji'* in the Madinan Adhan according to the Maliki school?
   (A) Pronouncing the opening Takbir four times at high volume
   (B) Calling the Adhan in complete silence without moving the lips
   (C) Reciting the Iqamah in a single continuous breath without stopping
   (D) Uttering the two testimonies of faith softly to oneself before repeating them aloud at full volume

   (A) Complete the final Tashahhud, say Salam, prostrate twice, recite a second Tashahhud, and say Salam again
   (B) Complete the final Tashahhud, perform two prostrations before the Salam, rise and immediately say Salam without reciting a second Tashahhud
   (C) Stand up immediately after the final rak'ah and pray a complete extra rak'ah
   (D) Prostrate four times before the Tashahhud and give charity

   (A) Sit back down immediately even after standing straight, and repeat the Tashahhud
   (B) Break the prayer immediately and start again from the opening Takbir
   (C) Continue standing, complete the remaining units of prayer, and perform Sujud al-Qabli before the final Salam
   (D) Finish the prayer normally and perform Sujud al-Ba'di after the final Salam

   (A) When an accidental addition (*Ziyadah*, such as an extra bowing or prostration) occurred during the prayer
   (B) When two or more confirmed Sunnahs were omitted from the prayer
   (C) Before reciting the Fatihah in the first rak'ah
   (D) Whenever the worshipper feels tired during voluntary prayers

    (C) Wiping only the right side of the head and the ear
    (D) Pouring a cup of water over the head without touching it

* Sujud al-Qabli ─── Two prostrations before Salam to repair omissions of Sunnahs

| **Classical Text Spine** | *Al-Risalah* of Imam Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani (Chapters on Taharah & Salah) and *Matn Ibn 'Ashir* |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 10: "Allah is Pure and Accepts Only What Is Pure" (Sahih Muslim 1015) |

---

## Section 1: The Conditions of Prayer: Obligation versus Validity

As young Muslims reach adolescence and physical maturity (*Bulugh*), the sacred law (*Shari'ah*) addresses them as morally accountable individuals (*Mukallafun*). In classical Maliki jurisprudence, the prerequisites of prayer are divided into two categories:

### 1. Conditions of Obligation (*Shurut al-Wujub*):
These conditions dictate who is legally required to pray:
* **Islam:** Being a Muslim.
* **Puberty (*Bulugh*):** Reaching physical maturity through biological signs or reaching fifteen lunar years.
* **Sanity (*'Aql*):** Possessing sound mental capacity.
* **Freedom from Menstruation and Post-Natal Bleeding (*Al-Naqa' min al-Hayd wal-Nifas*):** For young women, prayer is neither obligatory nor permitted during active bleeding; once bleeding completely ceases, Ghusl is performed and prayers resume immediately without making up missed prayers.
* **Entry of the Prayer Time (*Dukhul al-Waqt*):** An obligation only attaches once its prescribed time begins.

### 2. Conditions of Validity (*Shurut al-Sihhah*):
These conditions dictate whether a prayer is accepted as legally valid:
* **Purity from Ritual Impurities (*Taharat al-Hadath*):** Minor impurity removed via Wudu, major impurity removed via Ghusl (or Tayammum when legally justified).
* **Purity from Physical Filth (*Taharat al-Khabath*):** Ensuring body, clothes, and praying surface are free from unexcused impurities.
* **Covering the 'Awrah (*Satr al-'Awrah*):**
  * *For Men:* The minimum area from the navel to the knee.
  * *For Women:* The entire body except the face and the hands.
* **Facing the Qiblah (*Istiqbal al-Qiblah*):** Directing the chest toward the Ka'bah.
* **The Opening Intention (*Al-Niyyah*):** Explicitly intending the specific prayer concurrent with the opening Takbir.

---

## Section 2: Travel Concessions: Shortening (Qasr) and Combining (Jam')

Islam balances devotion with divine ease (*Rukhsah*). Allah states in the Qur'an:  
*"Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship."* (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185).

| Concession | Legal Rulings in the Maliki School |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Shortening (*Al-Qasr*)** | Shortening the four-rak'ah obligatory prayers (Dhuhr, 'Asr, and 'Isha) to **two rak'ahs**. |
| **Distance Requirement** | The journey must be at least **four Barids** (approximately 48 Arabian miles, equal to 77-80 kilometers or 48 miles) one way. |
| **Lawful Journey** | The journey must be for a permissible purpose (such as education, work, family visitation, or pilgrimage). |
| **Departure Boundary** | Shortening begins only after passing beyond the outermost residential buildings of your home town or city. |
| **Length of Stay** | If you intend to stay at your destination for **four full days or more** (20 obligatory prayers), you pray complete prayers (*Itmam*) upon arrival. If you intend to stay less than four days, you shorten throughout your stay. |
| **Prayers Not Shortened** | **Fajr** (2 rak'ahs) and **Maghrib** (3 rak'ahs) are never shortened under any circumstance. |
| **Combining Prayers (*Al-Jam'*)** | Combining Dhuhr with 'Asr, or Maghrib with 'Isha (either early at the first prayer time, *Jam' Taqdim*, or late at the second prayer time, *Jam' Ta'khir*). Permitted while actively traveling on the road, during severe rain and mud at the mosque, and at 'Arafah and Muzdalifah during Hajj. |

---

## Section 3: Wiping Over Leather Footwear (Khuffayn) and Bandages (Jaba'ir)

### 1. Wiping Over Leather Footwear (*Mash 'ala al-Khuffayn*):
Wiping over footwear is an established Sunnah confirmed by dozens of Companions of the Prophet ﷺ:
* **Conditions of Validity:**
  1. The socks or boots must be made of pure leather or durable, water-impermeable material that can withstand continuous walking.
  2. They must cover the feet completely up to and including the ankle-bones.
  3. They must be put on while in a state of **complete ritual purity established by washing with water** (not Tayammum).
* **The Method of Wiping:** Place the right moistened hand on the top of the foot and the left hand beneath the sole, drawing the hands across the foot once from the toes toward the ankle.
* **Duration in Maliki Fiqh:** Unlike other schools that restrict wiping to 24 hours for residents and 72 hours for travelers, Imam Malik held that a person may continue wiping without a fixed time limit, provided they do not remove the footwear and do not enter a state of major ritual impurity (*Janabah*).

### 2. Medical Bandages and Splints (*Al-Jaba'ir*):
If a person has a bone fracture, cast, surgical stitches, or open wound covered by a bandage:
* The patient does not remove the cast or bandage if doing so would cause pain, harm, or delay healing.
* When performing wudu, they wash all healthy limbs, moisten their hands, and gently wipe over the exterior of the bandage (*Al-Mash 'ala al-Jaba'ir*).
* This concession is valid even if the cast was applied while not in a state of wudu, based on the Islamic legal maxim: *"Harm must be eliminated"* (*Al-Dararu Yuzal*).

---

## Section 4: The Maliki Tradition of Sadl and 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah

In the Maliki school, the relied-upon and prevalent position for standing in obligatory prayers is **Sadl** (allowing the arms to hang naturally at the sides).

### Why do Malikis practice Sadl?
1. **The Proof of 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah (Communal Practice):** Imam Malik witnessed thousands of the grandchildren and senior students of the Companions in Madinah standing before Allah with their arms naturally draped at their sides. In Maliki jurisprudence, an uninterrupted, mass communal practice (*Tawatur 'Amali*) in the Prophet's city is a stronger proof of the Sunnah than an isolated individual transmission (*Khabar al-Ahad*).
2. **The Posture of Natural Humility:** Letting the limbs rest freely at the sides embodies quiet dignity, ease, and total physical submission.
3. **Respecting Scholarly Diversity (*Adab al-Ikhtilaf*):** Clasping the right hand over the left (*Qabd*) is also an authentic Sunni practice supported by authentic hadiths. In the Maliki school, *Qabd* is permitted in voluntary prayers. All four Sunni Imams agree that both *Sadl* and *Qabd* are valid, acceptable Sunnahs. Neither posture invalidates prayer, and Muslims must always pray side-by-side with brotherhood, respect, and mutual love.

---

## Section 5: Congregational Prayer, Friday Prayer, and Special Circumstances

### 1. Congregational Prayer (*Salat al-Jama'ah*):
Praying in congregation is an emphasized Sunnah for men in the mosque.  
* **Catching a Rak'ah (*Idrak al-Rak'ah*):** A latecomer (*Masbuq*) is counted as having caught a rak'ah if they join the Imam and achieve steady, tranquil bowing (*Ruku'*) alongside him before the Imam begins rising from bowing.
* **Completing Missed Units:** After the Imam says the final Salam, the latecomer stands up without an additional Takbir (unless they missed an entire rak'ah) and completes missed units according to the rule:
  * In recitation: they treat what they pray now as the beginning (*Qada'* in words: reciting Fatihah and a Surah aloud or quietly as appropriate).
  * In physical movements: they treat what they already prayed with the Imam as the beginning (*Bina'* in actions).

### 2. Friday Prayer (*Salat al-Jumu'ah*):
Friday prayer is an individual obligation (*Fard 'Ayn*) upon adult, resident, healthy Muslim men:
* Replaces the Dhuhr prayer with two rak'ahs recited aloud preceded by two sermons (*Khutbatayn*).
* Listening to the Khutbah silently is obligatory; speaking during the sermon is strictly prohibited.

### 3. Prayer of the Sick (*Salat al-Marid*):
A Muslim never abandons prayer due to illness. A patient prays standing if able; if unable to stand, they pray sitting; if unable to sit, they pray lying on their right side facing the Qiblah, gesturing with their head for bowing and prostration.

---

## Section 6: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 1. Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Haqqah (69:13-24)
Allah describes the Day when our deeds will be presented:

> **يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ**  
> *Yawma'idhin tu'raduna la takhfa minkum khafiyah.*  
> *"On that Day you will be exhibited; not a single secret of yours will remain hidden."* (Surah Al-Haqqah 69:18).

**Classical Tafsir (*Tafsir al-Qurtubi*):** Imam al-Qurtubi states that the believer who regularly stands in prayer with physical and internal purity will find their record of deeds delivered into their right hand with joy on that Day.

### 2. Tajweed Rule in Action: The Rules of Meem Sakinah
When a Meem Sakinah (مْ: a Meem with a Sukun) meets another Arabic letter, three rules apply:
1. **Ikhfa' Shafawi (Lip Concealment):** When Meem Sakinah meets the letter Ba (ب). The lips close gently with a two-count nasal hum (*Ghunnah*). Example: **تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ** (*tarmihim bi-hijarah*).
2. **Idgham Shafawi / Mithlayn (Lip Merging):** When Meem Sakinah meets another Meem (م). The two merge with a complete nasal hum. Example: **لَهُم مَّا يَشَاءُونَ** (*lahum-ma yasha'un*).
3. **Izhar Shafawi (Lip Clarity):** When Meem Sakinah meets any of the remaining 26 letters. The Meem is pronounced clearly without extra nasal stretch. Example: **أَلَمْ تَرَ** (*alam tara*). Extra care is taken before Waw (و) and Fa (ف) so the Meem is not mistakenly hidden.

### 3. Classical Maliki Text Anchor: *Al-Risalah* of Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani
Imam Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani (d. 386 AH) writes in his celebrated manual *Al-Risalah*:
> *"Shortening the prayer during travel is a confirmed Sunnah. A person shortens four-rak'ah prayers to two units over a distance of four Barids, which is forty-eight miles. Shortening begins when one leaves behind the residential buildings of one's city. If one intends to reside at one's destination for four days, one completes the prayers upon arrival."*

### 4. Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 10 of Nawawi's 40
The Prophet ﷺ said:

> **إِنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ أَمَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِمَا أَمَرَ بِهِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ**  
> *"Indeed, Allah is Pure, and He accepts only what is pure. And Allah has commanded the believers with that which He commanded the Messengers."* (Sahih Muslim 1015, Sahih).

**Family Application:** Purity applies to everything we touch: our bodies through wudu, our wealth through honest work and avoiding interest, and our family interactions through truthfulness and respect. When youth practice travel concessions with confidence, they realize the beauty and flexibility of Islamic law in daily life.

# Level 5 Senior Seminar Guide: Purification & Prayer

| Metadata Field | Curriculum Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Target Age Group** | Ages 14-16+ (Senior High / Level 5 Capstone Track) |
| **Estimated Study Time** | 90-120 minutes |
| **Prerequisites** | Comprehensive grasp of intermediate Maliki fiqh, travel concessions, and comparative Sunni madhhab frameworks |
| **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6): The Legislative Architecture of Taharah |
| **Tajweed Rule** | Advanced Rules of Stopping and Starting (Ahkam al-Waqf wal-Ibtida': Waqf Lazim, Tam, Kafi, Hasan, Qabih) |
| **Classical Text Spine** | *Bidayat al-Mujtahid wa Nihayat al-Muqtasid* (Qadi Ibn Rushd), *Al-Muwatta* (Imam Malik), and *Al-Dhakhirah* (Imam Shihab al-Din al-Qarafi) |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 1 ("Actions are by Intentions") and Hadith 2 (Hadith of Jibril) |

---

## Section 1: The Epistemology of Ritual Law (Usul al-Taharah)

In advanced jurisprudence, ritual purity (*Taharah*) is analyzed through legal theory (*Usul al-Fiqh*). Scholars do not merely ask *"What is the rule?"*, but *"How was this rule extracted from the Arabic grammar of the revelation, the evidentiary weight of hadith transmissions, and the overarching objectives of Islamic law (Maqasid al-Shari'ah)?"*

### The Taxonomy of Water in Maliki Legal Theory
Imam Shihab al-Din al-Qarafi (d. 684 AH) in his legal encyclopedia *Al-Dhakhirah* details the three-fold classification of water:
1. **Absolute Water (*Al-Ma' al-Mutlaq*):** Water that remains upon its primordial, created nature without qualifying adjectives (e.g. rainwater, seawater, groundwater, glacial runoff). It possesses intrinsic purity (*Tahir fi Nafsihi*) and the legal capacity to purify other entities (*Mutahhir li-Ghayrihi*), lifting ritual impurity (*Hadath*) and removing physical filth (*Khabath*).
2. **Altered Clean Water (*Al-Ma' al-Mukhalat*):** Water whose fundamental characteristics (taste, color, or odor) have been permanently altered by a pure substance that does not naturally originate from water (such as soap, saffron, milk, or tea). In Maliki jurisprudence, this water retains physical cleanliness (*Tahir*), but forfeits the legal capacity to lift ritual hadath (*Ghayr Mutahhir*).
3. **Contaminated Impure Water (*Al-Ma' al-Mutanajjis*):** Water corrupted by an impure substance (*Najasah*) that changes its taste, color, or smell. It is strictly unlawful for worship and consumption.

---

## Section 2: Evidentiary Analysis: Why Does Imam Malik Mandate Al-Dalk (Rubbing)?

Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6) articulates the divine imperative:  
`يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ`  
*"O you who believe! When you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows..."*

### The Classical Linguistic and Juristic Debate in *Bidayat al-Mujtahid*:
Qadi Ibn Rushd (Averroes, d. 595 AH) explores the legal dispute between the Imams:
* **The Majority (*Al-Jamhur*: Abu Hanifah, Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad):**  
  Maintained that the classical Arabic verb *Ghasala* (غَسَلَ) denotes causing water to flow over an object (*Imrar al-Ma'*). Under this linguistic reading, if water covers every square millimeter of an arm without manual friction (such as submerging the limb in a flowing river or standing beneath a heavy shower), the obligation of washing is fully discharged.
* **Imam Malik and the Madinan Jurists:**  
  Demonstrated through classical Arabic lexicography and Prophetic practice that *Ghasl* requires both the application of water AND the physical passage of the hand over the limb (*Al-Imrar bil-Yad*). Pouring water passively without friction is designated in Arabic as *Al-Insibab* (pouring) or *Al-Dahn* (wetting/smearing), not *Ghasl*.  
  *Legal Consequence:* In Maliki jurisprudence, dipping a limb into water without rubbing does not constitute valid Wudu. *Al-Dalk* is an indispensable, non-negotiable pillar (*Fard*).

| Jurisprudential Issue | Maliki School | Shafi'i School | Hanafi School | Hanbali School |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Extent of Head Wiping** | Entire head (*Jami' al-Ra's*) | Any part (even 3 hairs) | One-quarter of head | Entire head |
| **Rubbing (*Al-Dalk*)** | Obligatory pillar (*Fard*) | Recommended Sunnah | Recommended Sunnah | Recommended Sunnah |
| **Continuity (*Al-Muwalat*)** | Obligatory pillar (*Fard*) | Recommended Sunnah | Recommended Sunnah | Obligatory pillar (*Fard*) |
| **Basmalah in Al-Fatihah** | Neither loud nor quiet in Fard | Obligatory verse of Fatihah | Quiet Sunnah before Fatihah | Quiet Sunnah before Fatihah |
| **Touch of Opposite Gender** | Breaks ONLY if with pleasure | Breaks unconditionally | Does not break wudu | Breaks if with desire |

---

## Section 3: The Hermeneutics of 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah Regarding Sadl

In *Bidayat al-Mujtahid*, Qadi Ibn Rushd provides an objective comparative analysis of hand placement (*Wad' al-Yadayn*) during the standing position (*Qiyam*):

1. **The Scriptural Evidence for Clasping (*Qabd*):**  
   Imam al-Bukhari records the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd (RA): *"The people were commanded that a man should place his right hand on his left forearm in prayer."*
2. **The Madinan Hermeneutical Counter-Weight:**  
   Imam Malik transmitted this narration himself in *Al-Muwatta*, proving beyond doubt that he knew the textual report. Yet, in his operational legal rulings, he maintained that **Sadl** (resting arms naturally at the sides) is the preferred posture in obligatory prayers. Why?
   * **The Epistemic Supremacy of 'Amal:** The Prophet ﷺ led thousands of Companions in prayer five times daily for an entire decade in Madinah. If clasping the hands had been an obligatory or exclusive Sunnah, the universal, continuous public practice of Madinah would have preserved it without divergence.
   * Instead, the foremost scholars among the Successors (*Tabi'un*) in Madinah (including Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and Ibn Sirin) were documented praying with their arms at their sides.
   * In Maliki legal theory (*Usul al-Fiqh*), **unbroken mass living practice (*Tawatur 'Amali*) takes epistemic precedence over isolated solitary narrations (*Khabar al-Ahad*)**, because mass communal transmission is immune to transmission errors, idiosyncratic narration slips, or unrecognized historical abrogations (*Naskh*).
   * Both postures are valid, recognized paths within Sunni orthodoxy.

---

## Section 4: Advanced Prayer Jurisprudence: Sujud al-Sahw and Funeral Rites

### 1. Complex Sujud al-Sahw Scenarios in Maliki Law:
* **The Rule of Compounding Errors:** If a praying person both omits a confirmed Sunnah (e.g. forgets the first Tashahhud) AND accidentally adds an extra physical movement (e.g. sits for an extra pause), **the omission (*Nuqsan*) takes legal precedence**. The worshipper performs **Sujud al-Qabli** before the final Salam.
* **The Mechanics of Qabli vs Ba'di:**
  * *Sujud al-Qabli:* Performed after the final Tashahhud, before Salam, with two prostrations, followed immediately by the final Salam without a second Tashahhud (*Matn Ibn 'Ashir*).
  * *Sujud al-Ba'di:* Performed after the final Salam, with two prostrations, followed by a second Tashahhud and a concluding Salam.

### 2. Funeral Rites (*Ahkam al-Jana'iz*):
The rights of a deceased Muslim upon the community are a communal obligation (*Fard Kifayah*):
* **Washing the Deceased (*Ghasl al-Mayyit*):** Washing the body with pure water and lotus/camphor leaves with utmost dignity and privacy.
* **Shrouding (*Al-Takfin*):** Enveloping the body in clean, unstitched white cloth (three sheets for men, five for women).
* **The Funeral Prayer (*Salat al-Janazah*):**
  * Performed entirely standing without Ruku' or Sujud.
  * Consists of **four Takbirs**:
    * 1st Takbir: Followed by praising Allah (and recitation of Surah Al-Fatihah).
    * 2nd Takbir: Followed by blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ (*Al-Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah*).
    * 3rd Takbir: Followed by sincere supplication for the deceased (*Du'a lil-Mayyit*).
    * 4th Takbir: Followed by a pause for general du'a and a single audible Salam to the right side (*Taslimah Wahidah*).
* **Burial (*Al-Dafn*):** Lowering the deceased gently into the grave (*Lahd*), laying them upon their right side facing the Qiblah.

---

## Section 5: Modern Bio-Medical Jurisprudence & Hospital Worship

Senior students preparing for university and professional life must understand how classical legal maxims apply to modern healthcare realities:

### 1. Hemodialysis and Ritual Purity:
Hemodialysis extracts blood through an arteriovenous fistula, circulates it through an artificial dialysis membrane, and returns it to the bloodstream.  
* *Maliki Legal Analysis:* Blood circulation through an external machine does not break Wudu. In Maliki fiqh, blood exiting and re-entering the body from non-private passages does not invalidate ritual purity.

### 2. Colostomy Appliances and Chronic Incontinence:
Patients with permanent or temporary bowel/bladder stoma appliances are governed by the jurisprudence of **Chronic Discharge (*Salas*)**:
* They clean the appliance area, perform Wudu once after the entry of each prayer time, and pray their obligatory and voluntary prayers freely, regardless of involuntary leakage during the prayer window.

### 3. Medical Dressings and Orthopedic Splints (*Al-Jaba'ir*):
* Medical casts, sterile wound dressings, and orthopedic splints are gently wiped over with moist hands (*Al-Mash 'ala al-Jaba'ir*) without removal.
* This dispensation is grounded in the universal legal maxim: *"Harm must be removed"* (*Al-Dararu Yuzal*) and *"Hardship brings about ease"* (*Al-Mashaqqah Tajlib al-Taysir*).

### 4. Critical Care / ICU Protocols:
An immobilized intensive care patient unable to access water or move limbs:
* Performs Tayammum if an assistant can present a clean stone or bag of natural earth (*Sa'id*).
* If earth is medically prohibited or inaccessible, they pray within their capacity according to their current state (*Faqid al-Tahurayn*), moving the eyes or heart with intention. A Muslim never abandons prayer while consciousness remains.

---

## Section 6: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 1. Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6)
Allah concludes the verse of purification with a profound statement of divine purpose:

> **مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ وَلَٰكِن يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ**  
> *Ma yuridu Allahu li-yaj'ala 'alaykum min harajin wa lakin yuridu li-yutahhirakum wa li-yutimma ni'matahu 'alaykum la'allakum tashkurun.*  
> *"Allah does not intend to place hardship upon you, but He intends to purify you and to complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful."* (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6).

**Classical Tafsir (*Tafsir al-Qurtubi*):** Imam al-Qurtubi remarks that this closing sentence reveals the core *Hikmah* (divine wisdom) of all ritual legislation: Allah does not impose worship as an arbitrary burden, but as a systematic elevation of the human being into spiritual and physical cleanliness.

### 2. Tajweed Rule in Action: Advanced Rules of Waqf and Ibtida'
In advanced recitation, knowing where to stop (*Waqf*) and resume (*Ibtida'*) preserves precise theological meaning:
* **Waqf Tam (Complete Stop):** Stopping on a word where the theme and grammatical structure are complete. Example: Stopping at the end of verses that conclude a legal decree.
* **Waqf Kafi (Sufficient Stop):** Stopping on a phrase that is structurally complete, though the thematic topic continues in the next phrase.
* **Waqf Hasan (Good Stop):** Stopping on a phrase that makes complete sense, but where resuming must begin from an earlier word due to grammatical attachment.
* **Waqf Qabih (Reprehensible Stop):** Stopping in a manner that distorts or corrupts the meaning, such as stopping on **لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ** (*Do not approach prayer*) without reciting **وَأَنتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ** (*while you are intoxicated*).

### 3. Classical Maliki Text Anchor: *Al-Dhakhirah* by Imam al-Qarafi
Imam Shihab al-Din al-Qarafi writes in *Al-Dhakhirah*:
> *"Ritual purification is an act of devoted obedience wherein the sacred law combines physical cleanliness with spiritual submission. The jurist must not confuse customary cleanliness with legal purification: legal purification requires intention, valid substance, and adherence to the authentic Sunnah."*

### 4. Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 1 of Nawawi's 40
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

> **إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى**  
> *"Actions are judged only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended."* (Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907, Sahih).

**Family Application:** Purity begins within the secret chamber of the heart. When young adults cultivate honest intentions in their studies, work, and worship, their entire life becomes an unbroken act of service to Allah and a source of guidance for their families and communities.
